free_tier.stated: Included free of charge for each domain: dual-stack anycast network, DNSSEC and DANE/TLSA, vanity NS, failover support, unlimited records and requests, 60 sec. TTL, REST API access

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object or record-size cap is stated on the first-party pages read; the free tier states unlimited records and requests
per_object_cap.notes: the word unlimited is the vendor's claim, not a measured value

retention.stated: unverified: the first-party pages read state no retention period or automatic deletion rule for zones or records; DNS records persist until the owner changes them
retention.notes: no zone-inactivity or expiry statement was found on the pages read

egress.terms: the free tier states unlimited DNS requests; paid plans are priced per zone and the pricing page carries no per-query or per-GB line

interface_detail: a REST API is included free of charge for each domain; the API uses HTTP Basic authentication, with the account email address sent as the user and an API key as the password, base64 encoded; the Swagger document is at https://rage4.com/swagger/index.html?urls.primaryName=dns-legacy; API keys are created under Profile/API keys with an optional IP ACL, and the control panel is at rage4.com/dnsmanager. Delegation uses ns1.r4ns.com and ns2.r4ns.net.
tooling: curl or any HTTP client against the REST API with HTTP Basic auth (email address as user, API key as password); the web control panel for manual edits
chaining: an authoritative anycast DNS service with GeoDNS, DNSSEC/DANE, vanity nameservers, failover and a 60-second TTL; it can act as primary with secondary DNS elsewhere, and the vendor sells a separate AnycastIP service for content, not DNS

limits.value: unlimited records and requests stated on the free tier

limits_note: the only other numeric value on the free-feature list is a 60-second TTL, which is a DNS caching value and not a storage, retention or request quota
binding_note: the first-party free-feature list states unlimited records and requests, so no documented quota binds at a typical single-domain scale; the 60-second TTL is a design value, not a quota

identity_cost.detail: the signup form at https://rage4.com/Secure/Register asks for an email address and a password, plus acceptance of the Terms and conditions and Privacy policy; it has no phone, card or identity-document field. The live URL answered HTTP 404 when read on 2026-11-19, so the form was read from a 2026-09-30 Wayback capture of the same first-party page (https://web.archive.org/web/20260930075401/https://rage4.com/secure/register). A card is used only on paid upgrades, where the first-party billing guide names Stripe as the sole payment provider, supporting cards and PayPal.

reliability_note: no outage was measured here; the vendor SLA, which excludes service during a trial period and accounts with overdue invoices, states 99.99 percent monthly availability, sub-300 ms responses in 95 percent of cases each month, and a service-plan extension as the only remedy, with claims by email within 120 hours
confidence_note: the pricing and free-feature page, the API and API-key guides, the nameserver guide, the SLA and the billing guide were captured and quoted from first-party pages. The signup form was read from a Wayback capture of the first-party page because the live address answered 404. No live DNS probe was run, so the rung stays documented.
